papers.title: Measurement-induced state transitions across the fluxonium qubit landscape
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms that limit high-fidelity readout in circuit quantum electrodynamics is essential for its optimization. Multi-photon resonances are understood to be a limiting factor, causing population transfer from the computational states to higher-energy states under drive. This effect, known as measurement-induced state transitions, has been extensively studied for the transmon qubit. While this exploration has begun for the fluxonium qubit, a systematic study of this effect is lacking. Here, we bridge this gap by theoretically studying measurement-induced state transitions in the fluxonium qubit over a wide range of parameters, comprising essentially all experimentally explored ranges. We find that lighter fluxoniums are less susceptible to these state transitions when compared to their heavier counterparts. We attribute this effect to the combination of lower density of multi-photon resonances, a smaller requisite coupling for a given dispersive shift, and a more harmonic-like structure of the charge operator. We confirm the validity of our analysis by performing time-dependent readout simulations. Finally, we consider the impact of the superinductor's array modes on measurement-induced state transitions over a large range of parameters.

summary.summary: This paper systematically studies measurement-induced state transitions (MIST) in fluxonium qubits across the experimentally explored parameter space using branch analysis over $2 	imes 10^6$ parameter combinations, finding that lighter fluxoniums ($E_J/E_L 	o 3$–$6$) are less susceptible to MIST than heavier ones. The authors identify three physical mechanisms responsible for this difference: lower density of multi-photon resonances, smaller required coupling for a target dispersive shift $ ar{ ar{ ar{ ar{ ar{}}}}}$, and more harmonic charge operator structure in light fluxoniums.
summary.motivation: Readout remains the slowest and lowest-fidelity operation in superconducting quantum processors, and while MIST has been extensively characterized for transmons, a systematic study of this effect across the full fluxonium parameter landscape is lacking despite fluxoniums demonstrating $T_1 \gtrsim 1$ ms and gate fidelities exceeding 99.9%, making them a serious alternative for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
summary.method: The authors performed branch analysis on the fluxonium-resonator Hamiltonian with capacitive coupling, extracting critical photon numbers $n_{\text{crit}}$ as the resonator photon number at which average fluxonium population reaches $\langle \hat{N}_f \rangle = 2$ (ground) or $3$ (excited); they also validated predictions with time-dependent master equation simulations and extended analysis to include superinductor array modes via Floquet branch analysis.
summary.result: Light fluxoniums achieve average critical photon numbers $\bar{n}_{\text{crit}} > 200$ over 700 MHz bandwidth (compared to $\bar{n}_{\text{crit}} \approx 10$–$30$ for heavy variants); time-dependent simulations demonstrate readout fidelity of $1 - \epsilon = 99.97\%$ at $\tau \sim 100$ ns integration time for optimal parameters, though residual leakage to states $|3_f\rangle$ and $|5_f\rangle$ remains at $\sim 0.3$–$0.6\%$ even without MIST-driven transitions.
